newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan prices seen firmer, upside limited.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan prices seen firmer, upside limited.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures are likely to be firmer next week, backed by a widespread perception that the markets bottomed out after the spot July contracts expired on July 25, traders said on Friday.
The upside potential, however, is expected to be limited with the approach of a sluggish summer holiday season, and lingering concerns about Asian currencies, especially the Thai baht, they said.
"A widespread view that the markets had bottomed out caused the price rises this week, and the firmer tone should remain intact next week," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
"The upside resistance for the benchmark rubber is seen at around 127 or 128 yen per kg. The resistance would be tough to break through, unless speculative buying interest grows," he said.

Traders said the usual sluggish summer holiday period, when physical buying tends to slacken, and concerns over the weaker baht, are likely to keep stop investors from making any active fresh purchases.
Benchmark January on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 124.7 yen per kg on Friday, against 121.5 yen on Thursday.
On the Kobe Rubber Exchange, benchmark January rubber was quoted at 124.0 yen per kg against 121.0 yen at the Thursday close.

Another technical analyst at a commodity brokerage house said the fall in TOCOM rubber open interest in recent days, despite the price gains, showed that private investors had little interest in rubber futures.
"The private investors are focusing on other commodities, such as more volatile grains and platinum group metals," he said.
TOCOM open interest in rubber futures fell to 115,814 lots as of July 31, after recovering above 120,000 lots in mid-July, TOCOM said.
Thai rubber offer prices to Japan were at 100.00 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on Friday, against 96.00 U.S. cents on July 25.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 127.0 yen per kg as of Friday, against 121.0 yen a week ago. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-7431
